A
young boy stands in front of a fountain, eyes
wide with wonder as water curls around his
outstretched arms, leaving indelible marks on
not just his skin, but his very soul.
A wiry woman shouts at a room full of
students to repeat a combat drill, the rhythmic
swishing and pounding of dozens of staves
accompanied by the crackling feeling of gathering power.
A dragon-winged man slams his staff down onto snowy
ground, causing a storm of arrows to divert around him, the
few arrows that manage to strike true bouncing off of the
silvery scales that cover his body.
Hidden atop the snowy reaches of Mount Everest,
surrounded by an enchanted labyrinth of countless secrets,
lies an impossibly tall, black stone monolith: Ā'irī, School of
Spellstaffs. Though it appears to have no windows from the
outside, this is but an illusion that dissipates the moment you
step into it. The hallmark of Ā'irī is openness, with vaulted
ceilings, vast windows, and dizzying heights. Its students,
called Spellstaffs, blend spellcasting with martial prowess,
calling upon the power of the dragons roosting in Ā'irī to
guide them. While most of these students excel most in
combat, each of them carries a unique ability to see certain
events just before they happen, giving them an edge in nearly
any situation.
Draconic Blessings
Atop Ā'irī is the Ām̐ khā, or the Dragon's Eye. This strange
phenomenon is a beacon, attracting dragons from all over the
world and inspiring them to protect the students within.
Nobody is sure how it works, although legends have many
tales to tell.
Legend says that Ā'irī used to be an incredibly powerful
dragon who transfigured themself into Ā'irī to provide a
refuge for students of all walks of life, and the Ām̐ khā is the
manifestation of their soul. The Ām̐ khā, and the dragons it
attracts, infuses mages with unique power.
Life at Ā'irī
The curriculum at Ā'irī is esoteric, teaching students use
staves as opposed to wands, and though many witches and
wizards look down upon the Ā'irīkō for inferior spellcasting,
nobody holds these beliefs after seeing a master Spellstaff in
action. The program is eight years, with students separated
into houses based on various personality traits, and holds the
highest population of students throughout the world.
The sorting process includes the magical Scrivener's
Fountain that permanently paints the arms of the students
with sigils. The coloring of the tattoos – grey, blue, or white –
signifies the house.

Class Features
As a Spellstaff, you gain the following class features:
Hit Points
Hit Dice: 1d8 per Spellstaff level
Hit Points at 1st Level: 1d8 + your Constitution modifier
Hit Points at Higher Levels: 1d8 (or 5) + your Constitution
modifier per Spellstaff level after 1st.
Proficiencies
Weapons: Staves
Saving Throws: Wisdom, Strength
Skills: Choose two from Acrobatics, Athletics, Survival,
Herbology, and Magical Creatures.
Scrivener's Scrawlings
At 1st level, you undergo the sorting ritual at the Scrivening
Fountain, anchoring your soul to Ā'irī. The entity within the
Fountain paints your upper body with glyphs, sigils, and
patterns. These tattoo-like Scrawlings contain indecipherable
arcane knowledge about the past, present and future, often
changing while you sleep. When you finish a long rest, you
gain one skill or tool proficiency of your choice. You must
replace this proficiency with a different proficiency when you
finish a long rest.
Additionally, after 1 minute of touching the surface on
which a written language is written, your Scrawlings will
dissolve and reassemble into a translation of that text.
The Scrivener
The Scrivener is a far more present force at Ā'irī than the
Sorting Hat at Hogwarts. They’re a seer and a trickster, that
puts students in the houses they are destined to be in. They
travel through the secret passages that riddle the school,
playing tricks and speaking in riddles, but never doing harm.
The Scrawlings are the Scrivener looking into the student’s
past, present, and future and doodling the moments that stick
out the most – they’re just really good at doodling.
Dragon's Strike
Also at 1st level, the Dragonkeepers teach you ancient
techniques that are fueled by special Dragon's dice.
Maneuver. You learn two maneuvers of your choice. Many
maneuvers enhance an attack in some way. You can use only
one maneuver per attack. You learn two additional
maneuvers of your choice at 6th, 11th, and 15th level. Each
time you learn new maneuvers, you can also replace one
maneuver you know with a different one. At third level, you
must change any maneuvers you have to align with your
chosen staff, and new maneuvers must do the same.
Dragon's Dice. You have three Dragon's dice, which are
d8s. A Dragon's die is expended when you use it. You regain
all of your expended dice when you finish a short or long rest.
You gain another Dragon's die at 6th, 11th, and 15th level.
Saving Throws. Some of your maneuvers require your
target to make a saving throw to resist the maneuver's effects.
The saving throw DC is calculated as follows:
Maneuver save DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus +
your Wisdom modifier
Shielding Sigils
At 2nd level, your magic ripples along the runes emblazoned
on your skin. When you are hit by an attack or you fail a
saving throw, you can use your reaction to channel soul
magic into your Scrawlings, gaining a +2 bonus to your AC
against that attack or a +2 bonus to that saving throw. You
can only use this reaction while you are not incapacitated.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your
Wisdom modifier, and you regain all expended uses when you
finish a short or long rest.
Fighting Style
Also at 2nd level, You adopt a particular style of fighting as
your specialty. Choose one of the following options.
Blind Fighting. You have blindsight with a range of 10 feet.
Within that range, you can effectively see anything that isn't
behind total cover, even if you're blinded or in darkness.
Moreover, you can see an invisible creature within that range,
unless the creature successfully hides from you.
Defense. While you are wielding a staff, you gain a +1
bonus to AC.
Great Weapon Fighting. When you roll a 1 or 2 on a
damage die for an attack you make with a staff that you are
wielding with two hands, you can reroll the die and must use
the new roll, even if the new roll is a 1 or a 2.
Protection. When a creature you can see attacks a target
other than you that is within 5 feet of you, you can use your
reaction to impose disadvantage on the attack roll. You must
be wielding a staff.

Staves
Staves, though not widely used by the Western
wizarding world, are an important aspect of life at
Ā'irī. After a year of training in both types, students
pick one of two types of staves. Long Clawstaves
are more brutal, require raw strength and grit to
wield, and short, baton-like Scalestaves requires
more finesse, picking pressure points and striking
them with accuracy, not force.
Clawstaff
Melee weapon (simple, staff)
Damage: 1d6
Damage Type: Bludgeoning
Properties: Versatile (1d8)
Scalestaff
Melee weapon (martial, staff)
Damage: 1d6
Damage Type: Bludgeoning
Properties: Finesse

Spellcasting
By 2nd level, your connection to Ā'irī through your
Scrawlings solidifies enough to begin channeling spells
through your staff.
Spell Slots
The Spellstaff table shows how many spell slots you have to
cast your spells of 1st level and higher. To cast one of these
spells, you must expend a slot of the spell's level or higher.
You regain all expended spell slots when you finish a long
rest.
Spells Known
You learn the Atramento Caenum cantrip.
Additionally, you know two 1st-level spells of your choice
from the Spellstaff spell list.
The Spells Known column of the Spellstaff table shows
when you learn more Spellstaff spells of your choice. Each of
these spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots.
For instance, when you reach 5th level in this class, you can
learn one new spell of 1st or 2nd level.
Additionally, when you gain a level in this class, you can
choose one of the Spellstaff spells you know and replace it
with another spell from the Spellstaff spell list, which also
must be of a level for which you have spell slots.
Spellcasting Ability
Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for your Spellstaff spells.
You use your Wisdom whenever a spell refers to your
spellcasting ability. In addition, you use your Wisdom
modifier when setting the saving throw DC for a Spellstaff
spell you cast and when making an attack roll with one.
Spell save DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus +
your Wisdom modifier
Spell attack modifier = your proficiency bonus +
your Wisdom modifier
Spellcasting Focus
You can use a staff as a spellcasting focus for your Spellstaff
spells. A staff is not an implement widely used in the Western
world, but the isolation of Ā'irī paired with Mount Everest's
abundance of trees suitable for wandmaking have allowed
the practice to stick around for the students and graduates of
the school.
Ā'irīkō Staff
Beginning at 3rd level, your training with the staff allows you
to bond with a specific staff, learning to use it as an
inseperable extension of yourself. Choose a Clawstaff or a
Scalestaff, and bond it to become your Ā'irīkō Staff. It takes
on a unique characteristic, such as illusory flames or twisting
blackened runes, that dazzle the eye, granting you advantage
on Performance checks to flourish or otherwise entertain
with your Staff.
Additionally, you may use an action to summon your staff to
a free hand with an arcane command word set at the moment
of the Staff's bonding.
Draconic Mastery
At 3rd level, you choose to focus your studies on a particular
branch of study. Your choice grants you features at 3rd level
and again at 7th, 10th, 14th, and 20th level.
Ability Score Improvement
When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 12th, 16th, and
19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice
by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by
1. As normal, you can’t increase an ability score above 20
using this feature. Alternatively, you can choose a feat.
Martial Magic
Beginning at 5th level, you can attack twice, instead of once,
whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.
You can replace one of these attacks with a quick casting of
the Atramento Caenum spell, which only deals 1d4 radiant
damage when cast in this manner.
Improved Dragonstrikes
At 10th level, your mastery of the ancient draconic maneuvers
reaches new heights, and your Dragon's dice turn into d10s.
At 18th level, they turn into d12s.
Ā'irīkō Ascendance
Beginning at 11th level, your staff becomes an extension of
your very soul, as well as that of Ām̐ khā. As a free action, you
can cause your Ā'irīkō Staff to extend, spectral staff segments
granting it a melee range of 15'.
Additionally, when you use a maneuver granted by your
Dragon's Strike feature, you may deal radiant damage instead
of bludgeoning damage with the attack.
Soulbound Staff
Starting at 14th level, your Scrivener's Scrawlings truly
anchor you to Ā’irī, and your Ā’irīkō Staff to you. When you
are using your Shielding Sigils, the bonuses provided
increase to a +3 bonus to your AC against the triggering
attack or a +4 bonus to the triggering saving throw.
Additionally, your Staff cannot be broken, and you can
summon it wordlessly as a bonus action. If you do not have a
free hand, it floats beside you until you grab it.

Draconic Masteries
Upon binding their Ā'irīkō Staff, students prioritize one of
three Masteries: Soul, Body, or Mind.
Mastery of the Dragon's
Soul
Students of the Mastery of the Dragon's Soul channel the
radiant altruism of Ām̐ khā, the original primordial dragon
whose immortal soul powers Ā'irī. They become almost-holy
hunters of the profane, seeking out Dark wizards and beings
such as dementors and doing their utmost to stop them from
causing harm.
Soul Spells
Upon choosing this Mastery at 3rd level, you learn an
additional spell when you reach certain levels in this class, as
shown in the Soul Spells table. Each spell counts as a
Spellstaff spell for you, but it doesn't count against the
number of Spellstaff spells you know.

Binding Light
At 3rd level, the light of any magic resonates with the light of
Ām̐ khā within you. When you are in bright light from a
magical source and you hit a creature with a melee weapon
attack, the creature's speed is halved until the start of your
next turn.
Additionally, you can cast the lumos maxima spell once
without expending a spell slot. You must finish a long rest to
cast this spell again with this feature.
Soul Coalescence
Starting at 7th level, you can forge a soul bond among people
who are united by cause. Once per long rest as an action, you
choose a number of willing creatures within 30 feet of you
(this can include yourself) equal to your proficiency bonus.
You create a magical bond among them until you use this
feature again. While any bonded creature is within 30 feet of
another, the creature can roll a d4 and add the number rolled
to an attack roll, an ability check, or a saving throw it makes.
Each creature can add the d4 no more than once per turn.
Light Against Darkness
At 10th level, your pursuit of abhorrent magic has honed your
senses. You feel the faintest of shivers down your spine
whenever you come within 60 feet of a creature or place that
has been scarred, warped or otherwise touched by Dark
magic. You cannot determine the direction nor identify the
source of this magic, but if you come in direct physical
contact with the source, you will feel another shudder,
confirming Dark magic's influence.
Strength of Soul
At 15th level, creatures of darkness revile you, and you
become inured to their worst facets. Dark creatures have
disadvantage on attack rolls against you, and you can't be
charmed, frightened, or possessed by them.
Ām̐ khā's Aspect
At 20th level, you can tap into the raw power of the Dragon's
Eye wherever you are. As a bonus action, you gain the
following benefits for 1 minute:
Draconic wings sprout from your back and grant you a
flying speed of 60 feet.
Bright light shines from you in a 30-foot radius, and dim
light shines 30 feet beyond that.
Whenever an enemy creature starts its turn in the bright
light, the creature takes 10 radiant damage.
Once you use
this feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a long
rest, unless you expend a 5th-level spell slot to use it
again.

Mastery of the Dragon's
Body
Students of the Mastery of the Dragon's Body typically go on
to be defenders of the weak, protecting Muggle villages in the
Himalayas from that which they cannot understand. They
choose to focus on empowering their physical forms to better
reflect physical aspects of the dragons that roost at Ā'irī,
forgoing more powerful casting.
Body Spells
Upon choosing this Mastery at 3rd level, you learn an
additional spell when you reach certain levels in this class, as
shown in the Body Spells table. Each spell counts as a
Spellstaff spell for you, but it doesn't count against the
number of Spellstaff spells you know.

Strength of the Dragon
As Eyrian magic flows through your body, it causes physical
traits of Ā'irī's guardians to manifest. At 3rd level, your hit
point maximum increases by 3 and increases by 1 again
whenever you gain a level in this class.
Additionally, parts of your skin are covered by a thin sheen
of dragon-like scales. Your AC equals 13 + your Dexterity
modifier OR 13 + your Strength modifier.
Rule Tip: AC Calculations Don’t Stack
When the game gives you more than one way to calculate your
Armor Class, you can use only one of them. You choose the
one to use. For example, if you have the Strength of the
Dragon feature and are wearing a cloak, you don’t mix them
together. Instead, choose which one determines your AC.
Featherlight Step
At 7th level, combat drills on the sheer precipices of Ā’irī have
honed your balance to preternatural heights. Your speed
increases by 10 feet, and you can move along vertical
surfaces and across liquids on your turn without falling
during the move.
Wandering Defender
At 10th level, you've completed specialized training to live
among and protect Muggle communities. You gain expertise
with the Muggle Studies skill, which means your proficiency
bonus is doubled for any ability check you make with it.
Additionally, you can find a place to hide, rest, or
recuperate among both wizards and muggles, unless you
have shown yourself to be a danger to them.
Warding Wave
At 15th level, you can send out a blast of magic to soften
blows and weaken spells. If you or a creature you can see
within 5 feet of you is hit by an attack or spell, as a reaction
you can grant the target resistance against the attack or
spell's damage.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your
Wisdom modifier (a minimum of once), and you regain all
expended uses of it when you finish a long rest.
Dragon's Fury
At 20th level, you can center yourself, channeling your magic
to enter a state of heightened martial prowess. As a bonus
action, you gain the following benefits for 1 minute:
Once on each of your turns when you make a weapon
attack and miss, you can cause that attack to hit instead.
You have advantage on all Constitution, Dexterity, and
Strength saving throws.
Roll an extra damage die each time you hit with a staff
attack.
Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again until you
finish a long rest, unless you expend a 5th-level spell slot to
use it again.

Mastery of the Dragon's
Mind
Students of the Mastery of the Dragon's Mind focus, more
than anything, on emulating the mind of the dragon – the
sheer force of will that powers potent spellcasting as well as
quick reflexes and raw strength. There is no particular trend
in terms of chosen profession, as their more powerful
spellcasting allows them to interface on a more even level
with Western witches and wizards.
Mind Spells
Upon choosing this Mastery at 3rd level, you learn an
additional spell when you reach certain levels in this class, as
shown in the Mind Spells table. Each spell counts as a
Spellstaff spell for you, but it doesn't count against the
number of Spellstaff spells you know.

Spellslinger
At 3rd level, you learn two cantrips of your choice from the
Wands and Wizards spell list. They count as Spellstaff spells
for you, and Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for them.
Whenever you gain a level in this class, you can replace one
of these cantrips with another cantrip. You learn another
cantrip at 9th level, and again at 13th and 17th level.
Additionally, when you cast Atramento Caenum, the
damage dice are increased to d6's.
Cast 'n' Clobber
Beginning at 7th level, when you use your action to cast a
cantrip, you can make one weapon attack as a bonus action.
International Drakewarden
At 10th level, you've completed your studies of all species of
dragons all around the world. Whenever you make an
Intelligence (History of Magic) or Wisdom (Magical
Creatures) check related to dragons, you are considered
proficient in the applicable skill and add double your
proficiency bonus to the check, instead of your normal
proficiency bonus.
Additionally, you're fluent in 10 non-
magical languages of your choice.
Scrivener's Strike
Starting at 15th level, you've learned to "bleed" your
Scrivener's Scrawlings down your staff, sending their arcana
to systematically destroy another's. When you use your action
to cast a spell, you can make one staff attack as a bonus
action. This attack is infused with the full power of the
Scrivening Fountain, and scores a critical hit on a roll of 19
or 20. On a hit, you can also end one spell of your choice on
the target. The level of the spell you end must be equal to or
lower than the level of the spell slot you used as your action,
or twice that level if the attack was a critical hit.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your
Wisdom modifier, and regain uses of this feature at the end of
a long rest.
Ām̐ khā's Overcharge
At 20th level, you can temporarily blend spells and staff
mastery with perfect harmony. As a bonus action, you gain
the following benefits for 1 minute:
When you cast a spell that deals damage and isn't a
cantrip, you can deal maximum damage with that spell.
You take 1d20 necrotic damage for each level of the spell,
immediately after you cast it. This damage ignores
resistance and immunity.
When you use your action to cast a spell, you can make
one weapon attack as a bonus action.
When you hit a creature with a weapon attack, the first
time it makes a saving throw, it must roll a d4 and subtract
the number rolled from the save.
Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again until you
finish a long rest, unless you expend a 5th-level spell slot to
use it again.

Falling Hazard!
As a part of the sorting ceremony at the Scrivener's
Fountain, each student receives an item called a
Fallband, to protect them from falls in the
precarious halls of the Eyrie, as well as allow them
to enter the Muggle world without attracting too
much attention.
Fallband
Item Rarity: Uncommon
While wearing this metal bracelet finely engraved
with the symbols of your house, you can use the
arresto momentum spell at will, targeting only
yourself. Additionally, you can use an action to
magically hide your Scrivener's Scrawlings.

Spellstaff Spell List

Spellstaff Signature Spells
Atramento Caenum
The Inkmire Incantation – transfiguration cantrip
Casting Time: 1 action
Range: 15 feet
Duration: Instantaneous
You channel your Scrivener's Scrawlings down your staff,
spraying a gout of glowing ink towards a creature you see
within range. The target must succeed on a Dexterity saving
throw or take 1d4 radiant damage, and have its speed
reduced by 10 feet until the start of your next turn.
The spell's damage increases by 1d4 when you reach 5th
Level (2d4), 11th level (3d4), and 17th level (4d4).
Lumos Lamina
The Refraction Incantation – 1st-level transfiguration
Casting Time: 1 bonus action
Range: Self
Duration: Concentration, up to 1 minute
You transfigure the staff you're holding into one of solid
crystal, channelling the light of a dragon's soul through it.
Until the spell ends, your staff attacks deal and extra 1d4
radiant damage on a hit.
Celeria
The Dashing Charm – 1st-level charm
Casting Time: 1 bonus action
Range: Self
Duration: Concentration, up to 10 minutes
This spell allows you to move at an incredible pace. When
you cast this spell, and then as a bonus action on each of your
turns until the spell ends, you can take the Dash action.



Gravitaria
The Gravity Shift Charm – 2nd-level charm
Casting Time: 1 action
Range: Self (30 feet)
Duration: Instantaneous
Gravity shifts in a violent manner, changing your personal
definition of "down." Pick a creature or object within 30 feet
of you. You fall towards the target, and upon reaching it you
may make a single weapon attack against it. If the attack hits,
the weapon deals an extra 3d6 bludgeoning damage.
Regardless of whether the attack hits, gravity rights itself
after the impact, depositing you neatly on your feet next to
the target.
Draco Spiritum
The Dragon's Breath Invocation – 2nd-level charm
Casting Time: 1 bonus action
Range: Touch
Duration: Concentration, up to 1 minute
You touch one willing creature and imbue it with the power
of Ā'irī, allowing it to spew radiant energy from its mouth,
provided it has one. Until the spell ends, the creature can use
an action to exhale radiant energy in a 15-foot cone. Each
creature in that area must make a Dexterity saving throw,
taking 3d6 radiant damage on a failed save, or half as much
damage on a successful one.

Fulguria Gradus
The Hastening Charm – 3rd-level charm
Casting Time: 1 action
Range: 30 feet
Duration: Concentration, up to 1 minute
Choose a willing creature that you can see within range.
Until the spell ends, the target’s speed is doubled, it gains a
+2 bonus to AC, it has advantage on Dexterity saving throws,
and it gains an additional action on each of its turns. That
action can be used only to take the Attack (one weapon attack
only), Dash, Disengage, Hide, or Use an Object action.
When the spell ends, the target can’t move or take actions
until after its next turn, as a wave of lethargy sweeps over it.
Ām̐ khā Aplexum
The Draconic Embrace Charm – 3rd-level charm
Casting Time: 1 action
Range: Self
Duration: Concentration, up to 1 minute
Draconic power radiates from you in an aura with a 30-foot
radius, awakening boldness in friendly creatures. Until the
spell ends, the aura moves with you, centered on you. While
in the aura, each non-hostile creature in the aura (including
you) may deal an extra 1d4 radiant damage when it hits with
a weapon or spell attack.
Invito Spiritus Sublimis
The Greater Summons Ritual – 4th-level transfiguration
Casting Time: 10 minutes
Range: 30 feet
Duration: Instantaneous
You summon a spirit that assumes the form of a loyal,
majestic mount. Appearing in an unoccupied space within
range, the spirit takes on a form you choose: a griffon, a
pegasus, or a hippogriff. The creature has the statistics
provided in the Monster Book of Monsters for the chosen
form. Additionally, if it has an Intelligence score of 5 or lower,
its Intelligence becomes 6, and it gains the ability to
understand one language of your choice that you speak. You
control the mount in combat. While the mount is within 1
mile of you, you can communicate with it telepathically. While
mounted on it, you can make any spell you cast that targets
only you also target the mount. The mount disappears
temporarily when it drops to 0 hit points or when you dismiss
it as an action. Casting this spell again re—summons the
bonded mount, with all its hit points restored and any
conditions removed. You can’t have more than one mount
bonded by this spell or find steed at the same time. As an
action, you can release a mount from its bond, causing it to
disappear permanently. Whenever the mount disappears, it
leaves behind any objects it was wearing or carrying.
Apparitus Illisus
The Apparition Attack Hex – 5th-level hex
Casting Time: 1 action
Range: 30 feet
Duration: Instantaneous
You flourish the weapon used in the casting and then
vanish to strike like the wind. Choose up to five creatures you
can see within range. Make a melee spell attack against each
target. On a hit, a target takes 6d8 force damage.
You can then teleport to an unoccupied space you can see
within 5 feet of one of the targets you hit or missed.
Ā'irīkō Maneuvers
The following options are available to you as a part of your
Brandishing Strike feature. After choosing an Ā'irīkō Staff at
third level, your maneuvers must align with the chosen Staff.
Clawstaff Maneuvers
Brace
When a creature you can see moves into the reach you have
with the melee weapon you're wielding, you can use your
reaction to expend one Dragon's die and make one attack
against the creature, using that weapon. If the attack hits, add
the Spellstaff die to the weapon's damage roll.
Goading Attack
When you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can
expend one Dragon's die to attempt to goad the target into
attacking you. You add the Dragon's die to the attack's
damage roll, and the target must make a Wisdom saving
throw. On a failed save, the target has disadvantage on all
attack rolls against targets other than you until the end of
your next turn.
Grappling Strike
Immediately after you hit a creature with a melee attack on
your turn, you can expend one Dragon's die and then try to
grapple the target as a bonus action. Add the Dragon's die to
your Strength (Athletics) check.
Lunging Attack
When you make a melee weapon attack on your turn, you can
expend one Dragon's die to increase your reach for that
attack by 5 feet. If you hit, you add the Dragon's die to the
attack's damage roll.
Maneuvering Attack
When you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can
expend one Dragon's die to maneuver one of your comrades
into a more advantageous position. You add the Dragon's die
to the attack's damage roll, and you choose a friendly creature
who can see or hear you. That creature can use its reaction to
move up to half its speed without provoking opportunity
attacks from the target of your attack.

Menacing Attack
When you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can
expend one Dragon's die to attempt to frighten the target. You
add the Dragon's die to the attack's damage roll, and the
target must make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, it
is frightened of you until the end of your next turn.
Parry
When another creature damages you with a melee attack, you
can use your reaction and expend one Dragon's die to reduce
the damage by the number you roll on your Dragon's die +
your Dexterity modifier.
Pushing Attack
When you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can
expend one Dragon's die to attempt to drive the target back.
You add the Dragon's die to the attack's damage roll, and if
the target is Large or smaller, it must make a Strength saving
throw. On a failed save, you push the target up to 15 feet away
from you.
Sweeping Attack
When you hit a creature with a melee weapon attack, you can
expend one Dragon's die to attempt to damage another
creature with the same attack. Choose another creature
within 5 feet of the original target and within your reach. If
the original attack roll would hit the second creature, it takes
damage equal to the number you roll on your Dragon's die.
The damage is of the same type dealt by the original attack.
Trip Attack
When you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can
expend one Dragon's die to attempt to knock the target down.
You add the Dragon's die to the attack's damage roll, and if
the target is Large or smaller, it must make a Strength saving
throw. On a failed save, you knock the target prone.
Scalestaff Maneuvers
Ambush
When you make a Dexterity (Stealth) check or an initiative
roll, you can expend one Dragon's die and add the die to the
roll, provided you aren't incapacitated.
Bait and Switch
When you're within 5 feet of a creature on your turn, you can
expend one Dragon's die and switch places with that
creature, provided you spend at least 5 feet of movement and
the creature is willing and isn't incapacitated. This movement
doesn't provoke opportunity attacks.
Roll the Dragon's die. Until the start of your next turn, you
or the other creature (your choice) gains a bonus to AC equal
to the number rolled.
Commanding Presence
When you make a Charisma (Intimidation), a Charisma
(Performance), or a Charisma (Persuasion) check, you can
expend one Dragon's die and add it to the ability check.
Disarming Attack
When you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can
expend one Dragon's die to attempt to disarm the target,
forcing it to drop one item of your choice that it's holding. You
add the Dragon's die to the attack's damage roll, and the
target must make a Strength saving throw. On a failed save, it
drops the object you choose. The object lands at its feet.
Distracting Strike
When you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can
expend one Dragon's die to distract the creature, giving your
allies an opening. You add the Dragon's die to the attack's
damage roll. The next attack roll against the target by an
attacker other than you has advantage if the attack is made
before the start of your next turn.
Feinting Attack
You can expend one Dragon's die and use a bonus action on
your turn to feint, choosing one creature within 5 feet of you
as your target. You have advantage on your next attack roll
against that creature before the end of your turn. If that
attack hits, add the Dragon's die to the attack's damage roll.
Precision Attack
When you make a weapon attack roll against a creature, you
can expend one Dragon's die to add it to the roll. You can use
this maneuver before or after making the attack roll, but
before any effects of the attack are applied.
Rally
On your turn, you can use a bonus action and expend one
Dragon's die to bolster the resolve of one of your companions.
When you do so, choose a friendly creature who can see or
hear you. That creature gains temporary hit points equal to
the Dragon's die roll + your Charisma modifier.
Riposte
When a creature misses you with a melee attack, you can use
your reaction and expend one Dragon's die to make a melee
weapon attack against the creature. If you hit, you add the
Dragon's die to the attack's damage roll.
Tactical Assessment
When you make an Intelligence (Investigation), an
Intelligence (History), or a Wisdom (Insight) check, you can
expend one Dragon's die and add it to the ability check.
